scriptWithTimestamps:
00:00:00:00 - 00:00:02:04
Hashtags on Instagram. Chaos.

00:00:02:04 - 00:00:06:02
Anyone can turn any word into a hashtag,
but only a fraction of them

00:00:06:02 - 00:00:07:10
are actually used.

00:00:07:10 - 00:00:09:13
And those are the ones that driver each.

00:00:09:13 - 00:00:13:14
And the problem is, you can't see how many
posts a given hashtag has in total,

00:00:13:19 - 00:00:17:12
or which related hashtags exist
until you search for them one by one.

00:00:17:24 - 00:00:22:11
So most social media teams end up guessing
they pick hashtags based on instinct.

00:00:22:17 - 00:00:27:10
Copy what competitors use, rely on tools
that give Vegas instead of real data.

00:00:28:01 - 00:00:30:10
That's a problem
because choosing the right hashtag

00:00:30:10 - 00:00:33:10
is the difference between your content
getting buried or discovered.

00:00:33:11 - 00:00:36:23
But this isn't just about social
media managers planning their next post

00:00:36:23 - 00:00:39:11
or tracking the success of a campaign
launch.

00:00:39:11 - 00:00:42:09
Hashtags are often
where Instagram research begins.

00:00:42:09 - 00:00:45:02
If you're mapping a market
looking for creators, searching

00:00:45:02 - 00:00:48:09
for competitors,
or building an AI workflow around a topic,

00:00:48:15 - 00:00:51:03
you don't start with profiles,
but with hashtags.

00:00:51:03 - 00:00:54:20
The wrong starting hashtag leads
to shallow insights and incomplete data.

00:00:55:04 - 00:00:58:20
The right one unlocks the real
conversation happening around a topic.

00:00:59:09 - 00:01:00:06
This approach works

00:01:00:06 - 00:01:03:24
both for deciding what to post
and for deciding what to analyze.
